## 3. Runtime and constraints

Compiled by `pyc.py` for `py_core`; only this subset is allowed (anything else is rejected at compile time):

```text
ints, True/False/None, names, + - & | ^ << >> ~ unary -, not/and/or
  in conditions, one comparison per expression (< <= > >= == !=),
  mem32[addr] loads/stores (also mem32[a] op= v), name op= expr,
  if/elif/else, while/break/continue, pass, global, import (ignored).
  "from <name> import *" where <name>.py sits next to the source file
  inlines that file there (once), so firmware can be split into modules
  that share one global namespace; errors name the original file / line.
  Without such a file, "from <name> import *" reads the SystemVerilog
  package <name>.sv found next to the source or in a -I directory (the
  memory map packages, e.g. video_processor_map_pkg.sv): its
  "localparam ... NAME = expr;" lines become UPPER_CASE constants NAME
  (folded), "import <pkg>::*;" loads that package first, <pkg>::NAME and
  SV literals (32'h0001_0000, 'h40, 16'd10) are understood, so the
  firmware takes its addresses from the same file as the RTL decoders.
  UPPER_CASE module-level names bound once to a constant expression
  (or const(expr)) are folded at compile time.
  def f(a, b): ... return x   functions with positional parameters,
  called as f(x, y) in expressions or statements; recursion is allowed
  up to the core's call depth. Missing return -> None.
  A function passed to irq_handler() is an interrupt handler instead:
  no parameters, no return value, cannot be called directly.
Builtins: irq_handler(fn), irq_enable(), irq_disable(), wait_irq(), halt(value).
  wait_irq() (WAIT_IRQ, 0x3E) stops the core until its interrupt input is high (an enabled
  source pending at the intc), whether interrupts are enabled or not; with them disabled the
  code after it runs first (the race-free sleep: disable, test, wait_irq, enable).
Strings: a string literal (in any expression, e.g. puts("text")) is a
  small int handle; the text goes to a string table in flash at
  STR_BASE (0x8000), outside the boot image, for the firmware to read at
  run time through the flash controller. The table has 512 slots of 64
  bytes (0x8000-0xFFFF): [0] length (0..62), [1] 1 if the string
  continues in the next slot, [2..] the bytes. A handle is the first slot
  number; slots 128..255 are emitted as h - 256 so they fit LOAD_SMALL,
  slots 256..511 as h (a constant). Firmware decodes a handle with
  slot = h if h >= 256 else h & 255.
  strings("a", "b", ...) returns the handle of a block of consecutive
  one-slot strings (each <= 62 bytes), so handle + i selects entry i (a
  block never straddles slot 256, so the decoding holds for handle + i).
  Identical strings share slots.
Not in the hardware fast path (rejected): * / % ** on variables (py_core v1),
** always, default/keyword arguments, closures, lists, dicts, floats, classes.
--core 2 (py_core v2): * // % on variables (BINARY_MUL 0x17, BINARY_FLOORDIV
  0x1E, BINARY_MOD 0x1F: Python's floor division and modulo, a zero
  divisor traps), 256 globals and 32 locals per function.
```

- Register addresses come from the SystemVerilog map packages (`from <pkg> import *`), never hard-coded numbers, so firmware and RTL decoders share one source.
- Every hardware wait has a bound (poll count) and reports a timeout instead of hanging.

## 6. Function

Implement exactly this behaviour (from the reference program's documentation):

```text
video_processor firmware: symbol_overlay, the tracking boxes and the text.

Object c * NTR + k is the symbol of target k of object class c: every symbol the same size (17 x 17
pixels at 320, scaled with the frame: symbol_scale) on the target's predicted centre, whatever the target's size, 1 pixel wide, in
the class's colour (people white, ground transport red, aircraft green) and in the style chosen for
the class (camera register 0x51 + c, det_style): 0 dashed rectangle (dashes of 4), 1 solid
rectangle, 2 dashed circle, 3 solid circle (symbol_overlay shape 3: round the box centre, radius
half the larger side), 4 dashed oval, 5 solid oval (shape 3 with OVAL: an ellipse inside the box, so
a long vehicle gets a long oval), 6 a solid box on the target's centre, 7 dashed rectangle with
solid corners, 8 the same with a 2-pixel tick at the middle of each side pointing to the centre, 9
dashed triangle with solid vertices. Defaults (the testbench's): people (pedestrian, face) 7, ground
transport (automobile, vehicle) 8, aircraft 9. Each target has a label below its symbol (OBJ_LABEL,
the 3 x 5 font at 2x to 8x by the frame size, symbol_scale): P<n> a person (pedestrian, or a face not inside one; a face
inside a pedestrian's box carries the pedestrian's label and is drawn instead of the body), G<n>
ground transport, A<n> an aircraft (upper case: clearer in the 3 x 5 font), n the lowest number no
live target of the group has (1 to the number of the group's targets in the scene; a target keeps
its label while it is tracked). Pedestrians and faces are drawn on top of the vehicles (lower object
numbers). Texts (3 x 5 font, on a darkened backdrop): T_NAME the image name in the upper left
corner, T_CLOCK a clock (time since the core logic started, HH:MM:SS.mmm) in the upper right,
T_FRAME "Frame Number <n>" in the lower left, the number counted by the overlay itself at every
frame start (exact on every frame). Changes are committed (overlay_commit), so they apply whole at
the next frame start.
```

Per function:

```text
class_style: Symbol style of class c (det_style bits 4c+3..4c).

symbol_scale: Symbol, label and text sizes for the frame size: k = the longer side / 320 (rounded, at least 1);
symbols 2 x 8k + 1 pixels with lines (2k + 1) / 3 wide and dashes 4 to 16 pixels, labels 2x / 4x / 8x
the 3 x 5 font, texts 1x to 8x (so they read the same on a 320-pixel GIF and a 1920 x 1080 video).

class_shape: OBJ_CTRL of class c's symbols in its style, with the line width and dash length of the frame size.

class_ctrl: OBJ_CTRL of class c's style at the base size (1-pixel lines, dashes of 4).

obj_index: Overlay object number of class c's track k (c * NTR + k).

obj_addr: Base address of overlay object c * NTR + k (its OBJ_CTRL at + OBJ_CTRL): objects 16-31 are the
second bank (OBJ2_CTRL at 0x2A0).

obj_label: Register address of the label of overlay object c * NTR + k (OBJ_LABEL, or OBJ2_LABEL from 16).

number_label: OBJ_LABEL word: the letter then n (1-999) in decimal, first character in the low byte.

label_new: Target k of class c just confirmed at centre cx, cy (pixels): its label. A face inside a labelled
pedestrian's box, or just above it (the head over a dark body), takes the pedestrian's label (the
face is drawn, the body hidden: tracking.py next_box); otherwise the lowest number no live target
of its group has.

labels_used: Bit n set: a live target of the group starting at class g (people: pedestrian, face; ground:
automobile, vehicle; air: aircraft) other than target k0 of class c0 is labelled <letter><n>
(n 1-9).

overlay_setup: Overlay on: every target symbol of each selected class in its colour and hidden (no target
yet), no labels, the other classes' symbols off, the texts (texts_setup).

overlay_box: The symbol of class c's target k in the box x0..x1, y0..y1 (inside the frame) in the class's
style; applies at overlay_commit.

text_set: Text j at x, y (top-left corner) with ctrl (TXT_ON, TXT_FNUM, length << 8) at the text scale.

text_word: Characters 4q .. 4q+3 of text j (character 4q in the low byte).

div: v // d for v >= 0, d > 0 by shift and subtract (py_core has no divide); the remainder in rem.

two_digits: Characters of v (0-99) as two ASCII digits: tens in the low byte.

text_clock: T_CLOCK = HH:MM:SS.mmm of us microseconds.

texts_setup: Name (characters already written, name_len of them) upper left, clock upper right,
"frame number <n>" lower left counting from 1 at the next frame.
```
